GEO-NEW-20-012.explanation_en: IMD calls it a cloudburst when 100 mm or more falls in an hour over about 20–30 km². Spread evenly over a day, 100 mm means a much lower rainfall rate and less flash-flood risk; in one hour it can send a sudden flood down a steep valley.
GEO-NEW-20-012.explanation_te: IMD ప్రకారం సుమారు 20–30 km² ప్రాంతంలో గంటకు 100 mm లేదా ఎక్కువ పడితే Cloudburst. రోజంతా సమానంగా 100 mm పడితే వర్షపు రేటు తక్కువగా ఉండి ఆకస్మిక వరద ముప్పు తగ్గుతుంది; అదే గంటలో పడితే నిటారు లోయలో ఒక్కసారిగా వరద రావచ్చు.

option_explanations_en: The stem says the shaking was similar at both towns; magnitude and depth are already reflected in that shaking, so they do not explain the difference in loss.
Correct. With similar shaking, losses differ because of how many people and assets are exposed, how weak the buildings are and how well the town can respond.
A zone name describes long-term hazard of a region; it does not explain why two similarly shaken towns lost differently.
IMD colour codes are for weather warnings; they have no role in explaining earthquake losses.
No such legal condition exists; the need comes from residual risk.
An embankment reduces the chance of flooding; it does not make the river hazard stronger.
Embankments are built mainly along rivers to hold river floods; the claim that they protect only against coastal surge is wrong.
Correct. Overtopping, breach or drainage congestion can still flood the settlement, so warning and evacuation planning remain necessary.
